research_scope: Source-free independent Wave2 prerequisite identity review; source formulations retained and no meaning creation or certification.

aliases.reason: The going-up and going-down formulations' statement that a prime q of S lies above p of R under φ:R→S means φ^{-1}(q)=p, exactly the same prime-contraction operation underlying the relative-dimension and relative-assassin source contexts. Going up/down assert additional EXISTENCE of compatible prime ideals in chains and remain separate parent predicates.

Locally finite families and local Krull dimension take an open neighbourhood U of x, namely x∈U∈τ_X. This is exactly the open-neighborhood predicate already used for Hausdorff spaces and pointwise continuity, with British/American spellings only. No weaker arbitrary neighborhood notion is conflated: that broader concept remains missing. The finiteness and local-dimension conditions stay with their parent formulations.

The split-fibred-category source posits a base category C without a smallness hypothesis. Its prerequisite is the same ordinary category with objects, arrows, associative composition and identities as the size-unrestricted canonical candidate. The extra cleavage/splitting and Grothendieck construction are source-specific and no small-category condition is imported.

The categorical-fibre-product source requires an ordinary category possessing objects/arrows and composition, with no bound on its object collection. Its 'category and arrows' prerequisite is precisely the generic size-unrestricted category concept; existence and universal properties of this particular fibre product remain the parent meaning, not implied by category alone.

The filtered-category source starts with an arbitrary category I of objects, morphisms and their compositions; the displayed axioms make I nonempty and filtered but do not demand smallness. This is the ordinary size-unrestricted category prerequisite. Filteredness, nonemptiness and parallel-arrow equalization are parent conditions and not inferred for any general category.
